pages.hook: When an American friend invites you for dinner, the evening is relaxed and friendly. Knowing a few small habits helps you feel comfortable at the table.
pages.polite: Say **“Thanks for having me over!”** at the door or when you leave. Hosts love to hear it.

mythfact.s: A guest often brings a small gift, like dessert or flowers.
mythfact.why: It is common and polite, but it is not a strict rule.

mythfact.s: You should arrive two hours early.
mythfact.why: Arrive on time or a few minutes after. Too early can bother the host.

mythfact.s: “Help yourself” means you can take food on your own.
mythfact.why: The host invites you to serve yourself.

mythfact.s: Americans never say thank you after a dinner.
mythfact.why: A thank-you text or note the next day is very common.

lines: Hi! Dinner at my place on Friday?
We eat at 7. Please reply by Wednesday.

decode.why: Dinner is Friday at 7. Wednesday is the reply day.

compare.br: In Brazil a dinner invitation can start later, and the host often insists that you eat more.
compare.us: In the USA dinner often starts on time, and the host usually says “Help yourself” and lets you decide how much to eat.
compare.tip: It is fine to say “No, thanks, I’m full.” It is not rude if you are polite.
compare.ask: What would you bring to a dinner at a friend’s home? Say it in English.

quiz.q: A friend says “Dinner at my place?” You want to accept. You say…
quiz.why: I’d love to! is a warm yes.

quiz.q: The host says “Make yourself at home.” It means…
quiz.why: It means relax and feel welcome.

quiz.q: What can you ask before the dinner?
quiz.why: What should I bring? is polite.

pages.title: Reading quest — Friday dinner with Jordan · part 1
text: Today Jordan invited me to dinner at his apartment in Minneapolis. I answered, “**I’d love to! When?**” He said, “**Friday at seven**.” I asked, “**What should I bring?**” He laughed and said, “**Just yourself**.”
But I did not want to arrive with empty hands. I bought a small chocolate cake and a bunch of yellow flowers. At seven o’clock, I rang the bell. Jordan opened the door with a big smile.
I said, “**Thanks for having me over!**” “**Make yourself at home**,” he said. The apartment was small, but it was warm and clean. A candle was on the table, and I could smell garlic and tomatoes.

opts: A dinner at a friend’s apartment

tf.why: He answers “What should I bring?” this way.
He arrives at seven o’clock.
“Yes, I love pasta!”

tf.s: The writer does not thank Jordan.
tf.why: He says thanks and sends a text.

ctx.why: Empty hands = with nothing to give.

ctx.sent: The apartment was small, but it was warm and clean.

ctx.sent: It was a lovely night.
ctx.why: Lovely = very nice.

pages.title: Reading quest — Friday dinner with Jordan · part 2
text: Jordan asked, “**Do you like pasta?**” “**Yes, I love pasta!**” I answered. He put a big bowl on the table. “**Help yourself!**” he said. The sauce was simple, but I wanted more.
After dinner, we ate the cake and talked about our families and our jobs. At ten o’clock I said, “**Thanks for coming**,” and Jordan laughed. “I should say that to you!” he said.
On the way home, I sent a text: “Thank you so much. See you soon!” It was a lovely night.
